claim: March 2025 was a strong rainfall/flood episode supporting the observed road-disruption analysis.
Observed March-20 road closures caused a localized loss of modeled healthcare-network reachability.
The nominal newly unreachable population is ~4961, with sensitivity range 2554–5079.
The accessibility loss is spatially concentrated in Mukim Tebrau (85.4–94.4% of newly unreachable across sensitivity).
J105 and FT01 form the principal connectivity-critical recovery tier.
J105 is uniquely the most critical road under all spatial uncertainty.
CRPI identifies network-wide preparedness corridors by combining flood susceptibility and healthcare criticality.
CRPI is a calibrated flood probability or expected-loss model.
Nominal J105-first restores 64.9% of the initial modeled loss; J105+FT01 restore 90.7%.
The robust operational recovery policy is J105+FT01 first tier, then FT003.
The event produced a large citywide travel-time increase.
The study demonstrates spatially unequal resilience impacts despite small citywide mean delay.
